newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU offers accounting guidelines for EMU.
newsitem.headline: EU offers accounting guidelines for EMU.

text.p: The European Commission on Friday announced a series of accounting conventions for corporations to consider when drawing up financial statements in a single European currency.
"These guidelines give practical and comprehensive advice to standard setters and those that draw up and use company accounts," said Mario Monti, EU commissioner for financial services.
Among the many areas covered in the document, called, "Accounting for the introduction of the euro," the most important conclusions were the following:

-- "the introduction of the euro can be treated within the existing framework of European accounting legislation (notably the fourth Company Law Directive on annual accounts and the seventh Company Law Directive on consolidated accounts) and does not create a need for additional Community legislation."
-- "member states can use existing accounting practices which are allowed under current Accounting Directives to accomodate the changeover to the euro."

Several other important issues, such as the treatment of foreign exchange contracts, treatment of foreign currency translation differences in the consolidated accounts of firms and accounting for the costs of the changeover, are also addressed.
